text:
mryan: Running into a weird blocking behavior in the synchronous Python SDK stream iterator used in our sample app. close()/__exit__() sometimes blocks forever when the server closes after a final newline. This is hitting customers trying the quickstart and it's a painful onboarding friction.

mryan: Sync repro (very small):
```py
client = RedwoodSyncClient(api_key=os.getenv('TOKEN'))
with client.stream_chat(model='lite') as it:
    for msg in it:
        print(msg['text'])
# sometimes never exits the with-block even after server FIN
```

mryan: env: python 3.10, redwood-sync 0.9.3, requests-transport using urllib3, nginx ingress. Happened in both macOS and linux.

zara: Is this only sync? We fixed some async EOF-handling earlier but maybe sync path missed it. Any stack traces?

mryan: No exception. Hang point is inside Stream.__exit__ -> self._iter.close() where the close call blocks waiting for chunk read. Users see the UI spinner forever in the quickstart.

tom: We're inconsistent: async path uses aiohttp reader that we patched to treat EOF as delimiter; sync path uses raw socket read and newline parsing. If underlying read returns b'' we should synthesize final event. Looks like we didn't mirror that change.

eva: Also getting reports that the type hints in the sync client are confusing in the quickstart. The tutorial shows `Iterator[dict]` but IDEs suggest `Iterator[str]` for chunks; folks paste sample code and get lint errors. We should align typing across sync/async and docs.

mryan: Good point. The sample app in repo `examples/quickstart-python` uses: `for chunk in client.stream_chat(...):` and immediately treats chunk as dict. If typing is wrong, autocompletion breaks.

zara: Plan: (1) mirror EOF-as-empty-line fix in sync transport; (2) add a `Stream` object wrapper that has explicit `.close()` and `.cancel()` for sync and async; (3) fix type annotations to `Iterator[Dict[str, Any]]` and expose a `Chunk` TypedDict in top-level package so sample code can import types; (4) update quickstart docs.

tom: I'll pick up the sync EOF handling. Quick patch: when `recv()` returns b'' treat it like event delimiter and flush the buffer. Also add a small socket read timeout fallback so that close() won't block forever if remote stalls mid-frame.

eva: I'll update the typing PR to add `Chunk = TypedDict('Chunk', {'text': str, 'meta': Optional[Dict[str, Any]]})` and change return types to `Iterator[Chunk]` / `AsyncIterator[Chunk]`. That should make VS Code hints correct. 

mryan: For immediate mitigation, can we update the quickstart readme with a snippet showing a manual timeout wrapper? Eg:
```py
with client.stream_chat(...) as it:
    try:
        for ch in it:
            print(ch['text'])
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        it.close()
```
Not ideal but gives customers a way to bail.

ci-bot: CI: examples/quickstart-python tests failing (test_quickstart_exit) on linux-py310 (flake).

zara: Filed ticket RDW-DEVEX-219 to track: sync EOF handling + Stream API + typing + docs. Assigning to @tom and @eva. Adding test plan: simulate final newline-only chunk + immediate FIN, and simulate zero-length read with no trailing newline. Add integration test in examples CI.

tom: Will open a small PR that ports the async EOF fix to sync reader and adds a read-timeout parameter (default None) to the sync client constructor. Also will add unit tests simulating socket close semantics.

eva: I'll draft the typing PR and update quickstart example and README. Also will add a short troubleshooting note under "Streaming responses" about using `it.close()` and the temporary timeout workaround.

mryan: Thanks. Please ping this thread when PRs are up so I can validate on our ingress+proxy setup (we have an nginx with chunked buffering disabled). This is high-impact for first-run UX. :pray:

zara: cc @devex for docs and onboarding follow-up. We'll aim to have the sync fix and typings in the next patch release.

mryan: Leaving this thread here for follow-ups and test results.
